metaTitle: Home Inspection Company Marketing for Multi-Inspector Firms
metaDescription: Home inspection company marketing for multi-inspector firms: SEO, Local Services Ads, agent marketing and attribution across every inspector's calendar.
intro: Home inspection company marketing for a staffed, multi-inspector firm has two buyers to win: the homebuyer and the agent advising them. ASP runs SEO, Local Services Ads, Facebook ads and agent-facing marketing for larger inspection companies, and tracks bookings back to their source across all of your inspectors.

sections.heading: How home inspection demand works
paragraphs: Home inspectors work for buyers, so the pace of home sales sets the size of your market. NAR reported in October 2026 that existing-home sales ran at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million in September 2026, up 1.5 percent from August and down 2.2 percent from a year earlier.

The buyer pool is changing. First-time buyers fell to a record-low 21 percent share in NAR's 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers, and their typical age rose to 40. Federal law also directs HUD to tell potential homebuyers about the availability and importance of an independent home inspection.

Most inspection businesses are small. Census counted 7,496 building inspection services establishments with paid employees in 2023, a category broader than home inspection, and 6,424 of them had fewer than five employees. A firm with an office team and several inspectors has more to market: more service areas, more specialties and more credentialed inspectors to put in front of buyers and agents.

sections.heading: Marketing to real estate agents
paragraphs: Agents are part of most purchases. In NAR's 2025 Profile, 88 percent of buyers used an agent or broker, and 92 percent of buyers of previously owned homes relied on one. For a multi-inspector firm, agent relationships work as a channel of their own, next to search and ads.

We support that channel with assets your team can put in front of agents: inspector bios with licenses and credentials, an active Google Business Profile with current reviews, and email and social content agents can forward to their clients. Put each inspector's license on the bio. BLS says most states and localities require construction and building inspectors, the occupation that includes home inspectors, to hold a license or certification.

sections.heading: SEO and ads for inspection companies
paragraphs: On the search side, we build a page for each inspection service you sell, in order of what each booking is worth to you. Service-area pages cover the places your inspectors work, written with real local detail rather than copied city pages.

Home inspector is an eligible Local Services Ads category in the US, where Google runs it in your area. Google's screening for home inspectors lists general and professional liability insurance, plus state-level business and owner licenses where local law applies. LSA rank depends on review volume, response time and dispute rate, so the office team answering those leads is part of how the ad performs.

Google Search Ads cover searches Local Services Ads don't reach, and Facebook and Instagram keep your name in front of buyers and agents between transactions. The case study on this page is a multi-location inspection company where Facebook campaigns were rebuilt from the creative up, Local Services Ads were scaled across every service area, and YouTube, email and local SEO ran alongside.

sections.heading: Scheduling and attribution across multiple inspectors
paragraphs: With several inspectors and an office team, a lead passes through more hands before it becomes a booked inspection. Each marketing source and each office listing gets its own tracking number, website forms capture the campaign a visitor came from, and that source has to stay attached when your office books the job in your scheduling software.

The report then shows booked inspections and revenue by source, including Local Services Ads, Google Ads, organic search, Facebook and agent referrals, so budget follows what books. Tracking numbers get audited quarterly, because staff change, campaigns get added and numbers get reassigned. Where your software supports it, booked revenue goes back to Google Ads as an offline conversion.

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: Everything built for your inspection company stays with the company: the website and domain, each office's Google Business Profile and reviews, the ad accounts, call tracking data, customer records, and the video and email content we produce. Ad spend is paid from your accounts straight to Google and Meta, never through ASP, and there is no exit fee.

faqs.question: How do Local Services Ads work for an inspection company with several offices?
faqs.answer: Google asks businesses serving multiple locations for business- and employee-level licenses for each location. When one business has several locations serving the same area, Local Services shows only its highest-ranking ad for a search. Office coverage areas need planning before the profiles go live.

faqs.question: What credentials should go on our inspector bios?
faqs.answer: Each inspector's state license where your state requires one, plus any association credential they hold. For example, ASHI's Certified Inspector credential requires passing the National Home Inspector Examination, completing at least 250 fee-paid inspections that meet ASHI's Standards of Practice, and report review. ASHI has operated since 1976.

faqs.question: Can you market commercial inspections too?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can build commercial pages next to the residential ones. Those pages should name the standard behind the work, such as ASTM E2018, the standard guide for baseline property condition assessments of commercial real estate. InterNACHI has discontinued its commercial property inspection certification and now refers inspectors to the Certified Commercial Property Inspectors Association, so check which commercial credential each inspector holds before it goes on the site.

faqs.question: Why does response time matter for inspection leads?
faqs.answer: Google's Local Services Ads weigh response time and reviews when ranking, so slow replies can cost placement as well as the lead. With an office team, the fix is a clear owner for every new lead and a schedule that covers the hours leads come in.

faqs.question: What does marketing cost for a multi-inspector firm?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many offices, service areas and channels you run. ASP's Foundation tier is $2,500 a month, Growth is $3,850 a month, and Premier is priced to the engagement. The pricing page lists what each includes, and ad spend is paid to the platforms separately.

faqs.question: Does ASP own our ad accounts or reviews?
faqs.answer: No. They are set up in your company's name, and our What You Own page lists every asset.
